title: Äppelpannkaka (Apple Pancake)
description: Prepared with apples, flour, and salt.
steps: Sift the flour in a bowl and mix with salt.
Whisk the eggs with the milk and stir into the flour with vigorous whisking.
Let the batter stand for 1 hour so the flour can swell.
Peel the apples, cut into pieces, and fry in the butter with the sugar until almost soft.
Pour into the pan lined with cold butter, give the batter a vigorous whisking and pour over the apples.
Bake the pancake in a good but not too strong oven heat.
Turn out onto a plate and sprinkle with sugar.

title: Äppelpannkaka (Apple Pancake)
description: Prepared with apples, eggs, and milk.

ingredients.name: butter for the pan (30 gr.)
ingredients.sourceText: 1 1/2 tbsp. butter for the pan (30 gr.)

steps: Prepare the pancake batter as in recipe no. 769.
Peel the apples, cut them into thin wedges and fry them in butter along with sugar until they are half soft.
Heat a frying pan slowly, brush it with butter, and add the apples.
Whisk the batter vigorously and pour it over the apples, after which the pancake is baked in a warm oven until it is beautifully golden brown.
Turn it out onto a round dish and sprinkle with sugar.
This batch yields three large pancakes.

title: Äppelpasta (Apple Paste)
description: Prepared with apples, water, and sugar.

ingredients.name: sugar for every kg of apples
ingredients.sourceText: 0.5 kg sugar for every kg of apples

steps: Peel the apples, cut them into pieces, and remove the cores.
Place them together with the water and sugar and let them cook under constant stirring for 4-5 hours.
When the apples are completely cooked down and the sauce falls in flakes from the spoon, the paste is ready.

title: Äppelplättar (Apple Pancakes for 6 persons)
description: Prepared with cream, melted butter, and apples.

ingredients.name: 2 msk butter for the pan (40 g)
ingredients.sourceText: 2 msk butter for the pan (40 g)

ingredients.name: ½ tsk finely grated lemon zest (optional)
ingredients.sourceText: ½ tsk finely grated lemon zest (optional)

ingredients.name: 2 msk butter for the pan (40 g)
ingredients.sourceText: 2 msk butter for the pan (40 g)

steps: Prepare the pancake batter as in the previous recipe and let it rest and rise
Boil sugar and water to make a clear syrup, flavoured with lemon zest if desired
Peel the apples, remove the cores, and cut into 3 mm thick slices
Place the apple slices directly in the sugar syrup and cook until half soft
Heat the pan slowly, melt the butter in a water bath, and brush the pan with it
Stir the batter well and when it is poured on the pan, place one apple slice in each section
Fry the pancakes on both sides, place on a warm plate, sprinkle with sugar and serve hot without jam

title: Äppelpudding (Apple Pudding)
description: A pudding made with apple, cream, and lemon.
steps: Mix the applesauce with the grated lemon zest and with the gelatin dissolved in a little lukewarm water.
Last stir in carefully the cream beaten to stiff peaks.
Pour the mixture into a water-rinsed and sugared mold and set it out to stiffen.
When it is to be served, dip the mold briefly in lukewarm water, turn out the pudding and garnish with fruit and biscuits.

title: Äppelpudding med grädde (Apple Pudding with Cream)
description: A pudding made with apple, cream, and sweet almonds.

ingredients.name: boiling water for the gelatin
ingredients.sourceText: 3 tbsp. boiling water for the gelatin

steps: The apple sauce should be strained, quite firm and moderately sweet.
Blanch the almonds, dry them well in the oven, pass them through an almond mill and mix with the apple sauce together with the cream beaten to stiff peaks.
Last, add the rinsed gelatin dissolved in boiling water, which should be cooled.
Pour the mixture into a water-rinsed and sugar-sprinkled tin form and let it stand on ice for about 3 hours.
When the pudding is to be served, loosen it with a sharp knife around the edge of the form and turn it out onto a cake plate.
Garnish, if desired, with fruit and sponge cakes.

title: Äppelpyramid (Apple Pyramid)
description: Prepared with apples, almond, and sugar.
steps: Boil the sugar and water to make a clear syrup and let it cool.
Rinse the apples, dry them, peel them, and remove the cores with a corer.
Place the apples directly in the syrup and boil until they are soft and clear, then remove with a slotted spoon and arrange in a pyramid on a jelly dish.
If desired, fill the holes left by the cores with apple or red currant jelly.
Blanch the almond, cut it into fine cubes, lightly toast them in the oven, and sprinkle over the pyramid.
Serve warm or cold with whipped cream. If the pyramid is served cold, it can be garnished with 3 dcl. cream, beaten until stiff, if desired.

title: Äppelris (Apple Rice)
description: Prepared with rice, apples, and juice or lemon or vinegar.

ingredients.name: juice of 1/2 lemon or 1 tablespoon vinegar
ingredients.sourceText: juice of 1/2 lemon or 1 tablespoon vinegar

steps: Cook the apple compote as in recipe 820.
Treat and cook the rice grains as Indian rice (see recipe 795), but omit the salt.
When the grains are taken from the oven, mix them with the apple liquid.
Arrange the rice in a ring on a heat-proof dish or preferably on a silver dish.
Place the compote in a pyramid inside the rice.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff peaks form, gently fold in the sifted caster sugar.
Pipe the meringue mixture through a fluted piping bag over the apples.
Let the arrangement then stand in mild oven heat until the meringue is half-dry and has a light yellow color.
Serve warm or cold with whipped cream.

title: Äppelsnö (Apple Snow)
description: Prepared with apples, egg whites, and sugar.
steps: Wash the apples, dry them, place them in a small roasting pan and bake in the oven until they are soft, then pass them through a hair sieve.
Let the puree cool and then stir it with the egg whites and sugar until it is white and fluffy, or for approximately 2 hours.
Place in a compote bowl and let stand on ice for 1 hour.
Serve with biscuits or macaroons. The mixture can also be baked in the oven as a soufflé.

title: Äppelsoppa (Apple Soup)
description: A soup made with apples, lemon, and rice or potato flour.

ingredients.name: fresh or 300 g dried apples

ingredients.name: ½ deciliter French wine or sherry

Season the soup with the wine and serve preferably cold with whipped cream and rusks or toasted bread. If using dried apples, rinse these very well in lukewarm water and let them soak overnight in the water in which they are to be cooked.

title: Äppeltårta (Apple Cake for 12 persons)
description: A cake made with wheat flour, almond, and powdered sugar.
steps: From the butter, flour, the blanched and grated almond and sugar prepare a regular butter pastry, which is allowed to cool.
Peel the apples, cut them into sections and cook with the sugar and water to a compote, which is beaten up to cool.
Roll out the pastry to approximately 1/2 cm thickness.
In a form or baking pan bake a thin base of the pastry, which is allowed to cool.
Line the edges of the form with pastry, place the apple compote in, and fold the dough edges over the fruit.
Place the rest of the dough as a lid on the fruit and press well against the folded edge.
Bake the cake brown in moderate oven heat.
Remove from the form only after it has almost cooled completely, and serve with whipped cream or vanilla sauce.

title: Äppeltårtor (Apple Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with apples, butter, and sugar.
steps: Prepare the dough as in recipe no. 34.
Peel the apples, remove the cores with a melon baller, and cut the apples into thin slices.
Roll out the dough into a square of approximately 8 mm. thickness and cut in half with a wheel.
On one half, layer the apple slices alternating with sugar, brush the edge with water, place the other half of dough on top, and press the edges together well.
Bake in a warm oven until well-baked and the apples are soft, which is tested with a whisk.
When the cake is cold, cut it into 4 cm. wide and 8 cm. long pastries, which are sprinkled with icing sugar if desired.
This recipe makes approximately 18 pastries.

title: Äpplen med maräng (Apples with Meringue)
description: Prepared with apples, egg whites, and icing sugar.

ingredients.name: butter for the mold (10 grams)
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tablespoon butter for the mold (10 grams)

steps: The apples are washed, dried, peeled, cut into thin slices or dice and freed from the cores.
The butter is melted in a saucepan, the apple slices are added together with the sugar and shaken over heat until they are completely soft.
They are then placed in a buttered, ovenproof mold and allowed to cool.

For the meringue mixture, the egg whites are whipped until stiff peaks form, the icing sugar, which should be sifted, is folded in a little at a time into the egg white foam, and half of the mixture is spread over the apples.
The rest of the meringue mixture is piped through a piping bag in diagonal squares over the meringue.
The dish is baked in gentle oven heat until the meringue is half dry and has a pale yellow colour. It is then removed, allowed to cool and garnished in each square with apple or red currant jelly.
Serve with whipped cream.

title: Äpplen med ris (Apples with Rice)
description: Prepared with rice, apples, and egg whites.
steps: Rinse the rice in lukewarm water and place it on the stove in the boiling water with salt.
Let the rice cook vigorously for about 30 minutes, then drain it in a colander.
Set it aside from the heat to dry.
Stir the rice from time to time with a fork so that it does not stick together.
Peel the apples, cut them into wedges and remove the seed cavities.
Make a clear syrup from the sugar and water, place the apples in it and let them cook until soft.
Carefully place them in the middle of a dish and reduce the sugar syrup for a few minutes, then pour it over the fruit.
Arrange the cooked rice in a ring around the apples.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form, mix with the sugar and spread over the apples.
Place the dish in weak oven heat and let it stand until the meringue has taken on a light yellow color.
Serve the dish preferably cold with whipped cream.

title: Äpplen à la Tinesse (Apples à la Tinesse)
description: Prepared with apples, rusks, and sweet almonds.
steps: Dry and peel the apples and remove the seed cavities.
Melt the butter; crush the sugar so that it resembles pearl sugar; blanch and chop the almonds.
Mix the sugar, crushed rusks and almonds together.
Brush the apples with the butter and roll them in the mixture.
Butter a pie form with a little butter, place the apples in it and set in good oven heat.
When they are soft and have taken on a beautiful light brown color, place them on a glass dish and let them cool.
Serve with whipped cream or vanilla sauce.

title: Ärter inkokta på konservburkar (Canned Peas)
description: Prepared with peas and salt.

ingredients.name: Cold cooked salt brine (1 tablespoon salt per liter of water)
ingredients.sourceText: Cold cooked salt brine (1 tablespoon salt per liter of water)

steps: Shell the peas and separate the smaller ones from the larger ones, then rinse the peas. Place them in canning jars and cover with cold cooked salt brine (1 tablespoon salt per liter of water). Screw the jars shut or seal them and cook according to general rules for 1.5 to 1 hour, depending on the size of the peas.

Alternatively, the peas may be briefly blanched for 3 minutes in lightly salted water with a little sugar added before filling the jars. To preserve the color, add a knife's point of bicarbonate of soda and 1 bunch of parsley to the cooking water. Treat them as described above.

description: A soup made with peas, pork, and water.

Taste and adjust seasoning, then serve with the cut-up pork.

Cork the bottles and bind them well with parchment paper.

title: Ättikspäron (Vinegar Pears)
description: Prepared with pears, vinegar, and white wine.
steps: Peel the pears with thin, even peels, halve them if they are large, and remove the cores.
Scrape the stems well.
Layer the pears and sugar alternately in a jam pot.
Add the vinegar and wine, and let the pears simmer slowly with a tight-fitting lid until they are soft and clear, or approximately 2 1/2 hours.
During this time skim them when necessary.
Arrange them with a slotted spoon on a flat dish to cool and place them thereafter in a jar previously rinsed with brandy.
Let the syrup cook down without a lid until it is quite thick, then let it cool somewhat and pour it over the pears.

title: Ångstekt revbenspjäll (Steamed Spare Ribs)
description: Prepared with ribs, white pepper, and apples.
steps: Break the spare ribs, then wash them with a cloth dipped in hot water and rub them in with pepper and salt.
Rinse the apples and dry them well, remove the cores and cut them into slices, which are dipped in sugar.
Spread out the spare ribs with the bony side up and cover with apple slices and the rinsed prunes.
Roll it up and tie it in three places with sail twine, previously dipped in boiling water.
Brown the meat in a roasting pot, add boiling water and let it cook with a tightly fitted lid until the meat is tender, which takes about 2 hours.
Remove it, remove the sail twine, and cut the meat into nice pieces, which are placed high on a warm platter and garnished with apple slices and prunes.
Prepare the sauce according to general rules for sauces.

Prepare the sauce according to general rules for sauces.

title: Öllimpor (Beer Loaves)
description: Prepared with beer, wheat flour, and syrup.
steps: Boil the beer.
Stir half of the wheat flour with the milk and add with vigorous stirring.
Let the mixture boil well and remove from heat.
Add the syrup and spices, and when the mixture has cooled, work in the sifted rye flour and the yeast dissolved in a little lukewarm milk.
Work the dough smooth and glossy and place in a warm spot to rise to double size.
Then work it up with the rest of the wheat flour and let it rise again.
Then shape with wheat flour in the form of oblong or round loaves.
Place on heated and floured cloths to rise.
When well risen, place on buttered sheets, brush with cold water and bake in a warm oven.
During baking, brush the buns twice with hot water, likewise when the finished buns are removed from the oven.
Cover them well afterwards so that the crust does not become hard.

title: Ölsupa (Ale Soup)
description: A soup made with ale, syrup or sugar, and flour.
steps: Mix flour with 3 cups of milk and let it swell for about 1 hour.

Bring the ale to boil with the syrup and spices and pour into the gruel with vigorous whisking.
Serve the ale soup foaming.

title: Ölsupsbröd (Ale Soup Bread)
description: A soup made with wheat flour, rye, and yeast.
steps: In the milk whisk as much of the wheat flour as needed to make a thick paste.
Boil the drink, add the paste and let the mixture come to a good boil while stirring.
Pour it into a baking pan and stir in enough rye sifted flour to make a loose dough.
When this has cooled to about 40°, add the yeast mixed with salt and enough flour to make a quite firm dough, and let it rise to double its size.
Boil the syrup with the spices, allow it to cool and work it into the dough along with wheat flour so that the dough becomes firm.
Let it rise again, then treat, shape and bake as in recipe no. 939.

title: A Cheap Gravy For Hashes, &c.
description: A sauce made with bones, celery, and onion.

ingredients.name: Bones and trimmings of the cooked joint intended for hashing
ingredients.sourceText: Bones and trimmings of the cooked joint intended for hashing

ingredients.name: a small faggot of savoury herbs
ingredients.sourceText: a small faggot of savoury herbs

ingredients.name: sufficient boiling water to cover the bones
ingredients.sourceText: sufficient boiling water to cover the bones

steps: Chop the bones in small pieces, and put them in a stewpan, with the trimmings, salt, pepper, spice, herbs, and celery
Cover with boiling water, and let the whole simmer gently for 1-1/2 or 2 hours
Slice and fry the onion in the butter till it is of a pale brown, and mix it gradually with the gravy made from the bones
Boil for 1/4 hour, and strain into a basin
Put it back into the stewpan
Flavour with walnut pickle or ketchup, pickled-onion liquor, or any store sauce that may be preferred
Thicken with a little butter and flour, kneaded together on a plate
The gravy should just boil, to take off the rawness of the flour

title: A French Mode of Cooking Artichokes
description: Prepared with artichokes, melted butter, and water.

ingredients.name: To each 1/2 gallon of water allow 1 heaped tablespoonful of salt
ingredients.sourceText: To each 1/2 gallon of water allow 1 heaped tablespoonful of salt

ingredients.name: a large piece of cinder in a muslin bag
ingredients.sourceText: a large piece of cinder in a muslin bag

steps: Cut the ends of the leaves, as also the stems.
Put the artichokes into boiling water, with the above proportion of salt, pepper, herbs, and butter.
Let them boil quickly until tender, keeping the lid of the saucepan off.
When the leaves come out easily, they are cooked enough.
To keep them a beautiful green, put a large piece of cinder into a muslin bag, and let it boil with them.
Serve with plain melted butter.

title: A Good Beef Gravy for Poultry, Game, &c.
description: A sauce made with beef, shalot or onion, and sauce or mushroom ketchup.

ingredients.name: 1 tablespoonful of Harvey's sauce or mushroom ketchup
ingredients.sourceText: 1 tablespoonful of Harvey's sauce or mushroom ketchup

steps: Cut up the beef into small pieces, and put it, with the water, into a stewpan.
Add the shalot and seasoning, and simmer gently for 3 hours, taking care that it does not boil fast.

steps: Put the milk and butter into a saucepan, and shake it round over a fire until the butter is melted, but do not allow the milk to get very hot
Put the flour into a basin, stir to it the milk and butter, the yeast, and eggs, which should be well beaten
Form the whole into a smooth dough
Let it stand in a warm place, covered with a cloth, to rise

In the mean time pare, quarter, and core the apples, and boil them until tender in a syrup made with sugar and water in the above proportion

title: A Very Simple and Easy Method of Making a Very Superior Orange Wine
description: Prepared with oranges, sugar, and water.
steps: Break up the sugar into small pieces, and put it into a dry, sweet 9-gallon cask, placed in a cellar or other storehouse
Pare the peel of the oranges quite thin and put into one large pan or wooden keeler
Put the pulp after the juice has been squeezed from it into another large pan or wooden keeler
Strain the juice through a piece of double muslin, and put it into the cask with the sugar
Pour about 1-1/2 gallon of cold spring water on both the peels and pulp; let it stand for 24 hours, and then strain it into the cask
Add more water to the peels and pulp when this is done, and repeat the same process every day for a week
Apportion the quantity as nearly as possible to the seven days, and stir the contents of the cask each day
On the third day after the cask is full, that is, the tenth day after the commencement of making, the cask may be securely bunged down
Bottle it in 8 or 9 months, and it will be fit for use in a twelve month after the time of making

title: A Very Simple Apple Charlotte
description: Prepared with bread, apples, and lemon-peel.
steps: Butter a pie-dish.
Place a layer of bread and butter, without the crust, at the bottom; then a layer of apples, pared, cored, and cut into thin slices.
Sprinkle over these a portion of the lemon-peel and juice, and sweeten with moist sugar.
Place another layer of bread and butter, and then one of apples, proceeding in this manner until the dish is full.
Cover it up with the peel of the apples, to preserve the top from browning or burning.
Bake in a brisk oven for rather more than 3/4 hour.
Turn the charlotte on a dish, sprinkle sifted sugar over, and serve.

title: A Very Simple Method of Making Coffee
description: Prepared with coffee and water.

ingredients.name: 1/2 oz. or 1 tablespoonful of coffee per person
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 oz. or 1 tablespoonful of coffee per person

ingredients.name: 1 pint of water per oz. of coffee
ingredients.sourceText: 1 pint of water per oz. of coffee

steps: Have a small iron ring made to fit the top of the coffee-pot inside
To this ring sew a small muslin bag
Fit the bag into the pot and pour some boiling water in it
When the pot is well warmed, put the ground coffee into the bag
Pour over as much boiling water as is required and close the lid
When all the water has filtered through, remove the bag and send the coffee to table
Pour the water on the coffee gradually so that the infusion may be stronger
The bag must be well made so that none of the grounds escape through the seams

steps: Roll the paste out to the thickness of 1/4 inch, and, with a round fluted cutter, stamp out as many pieces as may be required

title: Almond Soup
description: A soup made with beef or veal, mutton, and vermicelli.

ingredients.name: lean beef or veal
ingredients.sourceText: 4 lbs. of lean beef or veal

ingredients.name: rather more than 2 quarts of water
ingredients.sourceText: rather more than 2 quarts of water

steps: Boil the beef, or veal, and the mutton, gently in water that will cover them, till the gravy is very strong, and the meat very tender
Strain off the gravy, and set it on the fire with the specified quantities of vermicelli, mace, and cloves, to 2 quarts
Let it boil till it has the flavour of the spices
Have ready the almonds, blanched and pounded very fine; the yolks of the eggs boiled hard
Mix the almonds, whilst pounding, with a little of the soup, lest the latter should grow oily
Pound them till they are a mere pulp, and keep adding to them, by degrees, a little soup until they are thoroughly mixed together
Let the soup be cool when mixing, and do it perfectly smooth
Strain it through a sieve, set it on the fire, stir frequently, and serve hot
Just before taking it up, add the cream

title: An Easy Method of Making a Charlotte-Aux-Pommes
description: Prepared with powdered sugar, raisin, and apple.
steps: Make a cake with the flour, butter, sugar, and baking-powder; moisten with the egg and sufficient milk to make it the proper consistency, and bake it in a round tin.
When cold, scoop out the middle, leaving a good thickness all round the sides, to prevent them breaking.

Take some of the scooped-out pieces, which should be trimmed into neat slices; lay them in the cake, and pour over sufficient raisin-wine, with the addition of a little brandy, if approved, to soak them well.
Place a layer of apple marmalade over the soaked cake, then a layer of cake and a layer of apples.
Whip the cream to a froth, mixing with it the sugar and lemon-juice.
Pile it on the top of the charlotte, and garnish it with pieces of clear apple jelly.
This dish is served cold, but may be eaten hot, by omitting the cream, and merely garnishing the top with bright jelly just before it is sent to table.

title: An Excellent Way of Preserving Cucumbers
description: Prepared with cucumbers, rind, and cabbage.
steps: Choose the greenest cucumbers, and those that are most free from seeds
Put them in strong salt and water, with a cabbage-leaf to keep them down
Tie a paper over them, and put them in a warm place till they are yellow
Wash them and set them over the fire in fresh water, with a very little salt, and another cabbage-leaf over them
Cover very closely, but take care they do not boil
If they are not a fine green, change the water again, cover them as before, and make them hot
When they are a good colour, take them off the fire and let them cool
Cut them in quarters, take out the seeds and pulp, and put them into cold water
Let them remain for 2 days, changing the water twice each day, to draw out the salt
Put the sugar, with 1/4 pint of water, in a saucepan over the fire
Remove the scum as it rises, and add the lemon-peel and ginger with the outside scraped off
When the syrup is tolerably thick, take it off the fire, and when cold, wipe the cucumbers dry, and put them in
Boil the syrup once in 2 or 3 days for 3 weeks
Strengthen it if required, and let it be quite cold before the cucumbers are put in

title: An Excellent Way to Cook a Breast of Mutton
description: Prepared with breast of mutton, onions, and green peas.
steps: Cut the mutton into pieces about 2 inches square, and let it be tolerably lean.
Put it into a stewpan, with a little fat or butter, and fry it of a nice brown.
Dredge in a little flour, slice the onions, and put it with the herbs in the stewpan.
Pour in sufficient water just to cover the meat, and simmer the whole gently until the mutton is tender.
Take out the meat, strain, and skim off all the fat from the gravy, and put both the meat and gravy back into the stewpan.

Add about a quart of young green peas, and let them boil gently until done. 2 or 3 slices of bacon added and stewed with the mutton give additional flavour; and, to insure the peas being a beautiful green colour, they may be boiled in water separately, and added to the stew at the moment of serving.

title: An Excellent Wine Sauce for Puddings
description: A sauce made with sherry or madeira, eggs, and flour.
steps: Put the butter and flour into a saucepan, and stir them over the fire until the former thickens; then add the sugar, salt, and wine, and mix these ingredients well together.

Separate the yolks from the whites of 4 eggs; beat up the former, and stir them briskly to the sauce; let it remain over the fire until it is on the point of simmering; but do not allow it to boil, or it will instantly curdle.
Serve separately, and not poured over the pudding.

title: An Unrivalled Plum-Pudding
description: A pudding made with raisins, currants, and sultana.

ingredients.name: the finest moist sugar
ingredients.sourceText: 2 lbs. of the finest moist sugar

steps: Stone and cut up the raisins, but do not chop them; wash and dry the currants, and cut the candied peel into thin slices.
Mix all the dry ingredients well together, and moisten with the eggs, which should be well beaten and strained, to the pudding.
Stir in the brandy, and, when all is thoroughly mixed, well butter and flour a stout new pudding-cloth.
Put in the pudding, tie it down very tightly and closely, boil from 6 to 8 hours, and serve with brandy-sauce.
A few sweet almonds, blanched and cut in strips, and stuck on the pudding, ornament it prettily.
This quantity may be divided and boiled in buttered moulds. For small families this is the most desirable way, as the above will be found to make a pudding of rather large dimensions.

title: Apple Fritters
description: Prepared with apples, lard or beef or dripping, and flour.
steps: Break the eggs and separate the whites from the yolks; beat them separately
Put the flour into a basin and stir in the melted butter
Add the salt and moisten with sufficient warm milk to make a batter that will drop from the spoon
Stir well and rub down any lumps
Add the whisked whites of eggs and beat up the batter for a few minutes
Peel and cut the apples into rather thick whole slices without dividing them
Stamp out the middle of each slice where the core is with a cutter
Throw the slices into the batter
Take out the pieces of apple one by one and fry them in hot lard until nice brown, turning when required
Lay them on blotting-paper before the fire to absorb the greasy moisture
Dish on a white d'oyley piled one above the other
Strew over them some pounded sugar and serve very hot

title: Apple Jam
description: A fruit preserve made with apples, rind, and juice.

ingredients.name: preserving-sugar per lb. of fruit
ingredients.sourceText: 3/4 lb. of preserving-sugar per lb. of fruit

steps: Peel the apples, core and slice them very thin, and be particular that they are all the same sort.
Put them into a jar, stand this in a saucepan of boiling water, and let the apples stew until quite tender.
Weigh the fruit, to ascertain the proportion of sugar that may be required.
Put the apples into a preserving-pan, crush the sugar to small lumps, and add it, with the grated lemon-rind and juice, to the apples.
Simmer these over the fire for 1/2 hour, reckoning from the time the jam begins to simmer properly; remove the scum as it rises.
When the jam is done, put it into pots for use.
Place a piece of oiled paper over the jam, and to exclude the air, cover the pots with tissue-paper dipped in the white of an egg, and stretched over the top.

title: Apple Jelly I
description: Prepared with apples, juice, and water.

ingredients.name: loaf sugar per quart of juice
ingredients.sourceText: 2 lbs. of loaf sugar per quart of juice

steps: Pare, core, and cut the apples into slices, and put them into a jar, with water in the above proportion.
Place them in a cool oven, with the jar well covered, and when the juice is thoroughly drawn and the apples are quite soft, strain them through a jelly-bag.
To every quart of juice allow 2 lbs. of loaf sugar, which should be crushed to small lumps, and put into a preserving-pan with the juice.
Boil these together for rather more than 1/2 hour, remove the scum as it rises.
Add the lemon-juice just before it is done, and put the jelly into pots for use.

title: Apple Jelly II
description: Prepared with apples, water, and sugar.

ingredients.name: loaf sugar per pint of syrup
ingredients.sourceText: 3/4 lb. of loaf sugar per pint of syrup

steps: Pare and cut the apples into pieces, remove the cores, and put them in a preserving-pan with sufficient cold water to cover them.
Let them boil for an hour; then drain the syrup from them through a hair sieve or jelly-bag, and measure the juice.
To every pint allow 3/4 lb. of loaf sugar, and boil these together for 3/4 hour, removing every particle of scum as it rises, and keeping the jelly well stirred, that it may not burn.
A little lemon-rind may be boiled with the apples, and a small quantity of strained lemon-juice may be put in the jelly just before it is done, when the flavour is liked.
Put it into small pots for storage.

title: Apple Tourte or Cake
description: A cake made with apples, rind, and cream or milk.

ingredients.name: good short crust No. 1211
ingredients.sourceText: 3/4 lb. of good short crust No. 1211

steps: Pare, core, and cut the apples into small pieces; put sufficient moist sugar to sweeten them into a basin.
Add the lemon-peel, which should be finely minced, and the cream.
Stir these ingredients well, whisk the eggs, and melt the butter.
Mix altogether, add the sliced apple, and let these be well stirred into the mixture.
Line a large round plate with the paste, place a narrow rim of the same round the outer edge, and lay the apples thickly in the middle.
Blanch the almonds, cut them into long shreds, and strew over the top of the apples.
Bake from 1/2 to 3/4 hour, taking care that the almonds do not get burnt.
When done, strew some sifted sugar over the top, and serve.

title: Apple Trifle
description: Prepared with apples, rind, and cream.
steps: Peel, core, and cut the apples into thin slices, and put them into a saucepan with 2 tablespoonfuls of water, the sugar, and minced lemon-rind
Boil all together until quite tender, and pulp the apples through a sieve
If they should not be quite sweet enough, add a little more sugar, and put them at the bottom of the dish to form a thick layer
Stir together the milk, cream, and eggs, with a little sugar, over the fire, and let the mixture thicken, but do not allow it to reach the boiling-point
When thick, take it off the fire
Let it cool a little, then pour it over the apples
Whip some cream with sugar, lemon-peel, &c., the same as for other trifles
Heap it high over the custard, and the dish is ready for table
It may be garnished as fancy dictates, with strips of bright apple jelly, slices of citron, &c.

title: Apples in Red Jelly
description: Prepared with apples, lemon, and gelatine.

ingredients.name: a few drops of prepared cochineal
ingredients.sourceText: a few drops of prepared cochineal

steps: Choose rather large apples
Peel them and take out the cores, either with a scoop or a small silver knife, and put into each apple 2 cloves and as much sifted sugar as they will hold
Place them, without touching each other, in a large pie-dish
Add more white sugar, the juice of 1 lemon, and 2 teacupfuls of water
Bake in the oven, with a dish over them, until they are done
Look at them frequently, and, as each apple is cooked, place it in a glass dish
When the apples are neatly arranged in the dish without touching each other, strain the liquor in which they have been stewing, into a lined saucepan
Add to it the rind of the lemon, and a tablespoonful of gelatine which has been previously dissolved in cold water, and, if not sweet, a little more sugar, and 6 cloves
Boil till quite clear
Colour with a few drops of prepared cochineal, and strain the jelly through a double muslin into a jug
Let it cool a little
Pour it into the dish round the apples
When quite cold, garnish the tops of the apples with a bright-coloured marmalade, a jelly, or the white of an egg, beaten to a strong froth, with a little sifted sugar

title: Apricot Cream
description: Prepared with apricots, isinglass, and sugar.
steps: Divide the apricots, take out the stones, and boil them in a syrup made with 1/4 lb. of sugar and 1/4 pint of water, until they form a thin marmalade, which rub through a sieve
Boil the milk with the other 1/4 lb. of sugar
Let it cool a little, then mix with it the yolks of eggs which have been previously well beaten
Put this mixture into a jug, place this jug in boiling water, and stir it one way over the fire until it thickens; but on no account let it boil
Strain through a sieve
Add the isinglass, previously boiled with a small quantity of water, and keep stirring it till nearly cold
Mix the cream with the apricots
Stir well, put it into an oiled mould, and, if convenient, set it on ice; at any rate, in a very cool place
It should turn out on the dish without any difficulty

title: Apricot Jam or Marmalade
description: A fruit preserve made with apricots and sugar.

ingredients.name: Ripe apricots, weighed after being skinned and stoned
ingredients.sourceText: Ripe apricots, weighed after being skinned and stoned

ingredients.name: Sugar, 1 lb. to every lb. of apricots
ingredients.sourceText: Sugar, 1 lb. to every lb. of apricots

steps: Pare the apricots, which should be ripe, as thinly as possible, break them in half, and remove the stones.
Weigh the fruit, and to every lb. allow the same proportion of loaf sugar.
Pound the sugar very finely in a mortar, strew it over the apricots, which should be placed on dishes, and let them remain for 12 hours.
Break the stones, blanch the kernels, and put them with the sugar and fruit into a preserving-pan.
Let these simmer very gently until clear; take out the pieces of apricot singly as they become so, and, as fast as the scum rises, carefully remove it.

Put the apricots into small jars, pour over them the syrup and kernels, cover the jam with pieces of paper dipped in the purest salad-oil, and stretch over the top of the jars tissue-paper, cut about 2 inches larger and brushed over with the white of an egg: when dry, it will be perfectly hard and air-tight.

Boil the asparagus in salt and water until three-parts done

Put it into a stewpan with the butter, parsley, and onions

Add the sugar

When boiled a short time and reduced, take out the parsley and onions
Thicken with the yolks of 2 eggs beaten with the cream
Add a seasoning of salt
When the whole is on the point of simmering, serve
Make the sauce sufficiently thick to adhere to the vegetable

Rub all through a tammy, and if not a very good colour, use a little spinach green.

title: Aspic, or Ornamental Savoury Jelly
description: Prepared with veal, ham, and trimmings.
steps: Lay the ham on the bottom of a stewpan, cut up the veal and cow-heel into small pieces, and lay them on the ham; add the poultry trimmings, vegetables, herbs, sherry, and water, and let the whole simmer very gently for 4 hours, carefully taking away all scum that may rise to the surface.
Strain through a fine sieve, and pour into an earthen pan to get cold.
Have ready a clean stewpan, put in the jelly, and be particular to leave the sediment behind, or it will not be clear.
Add the whites of 3 eggs, with salt and pepper, to clarify; keep stirring over the fire, till the whole becomes very white; then draw it to the side, and let it stand till clear.
When this is the case, strain it through a cloth or jelly-bag, and use it for moulding poultry, etc. Tarragon vinegar may be added to give an additional flavour.

title: Baked Bread-and-Butter Pudding
description: A pudding made with bread, currants, and vanilla or lemon-peel or nutmeg.

ingredients.name: 9 thin slices of bread and butter

Sweeten and flavour the milk, either by infusing a little lemon-peel in it, or by adding a few drops of essence of vanilla

title: Baked Carp
description: Prepared with carp, forcemeat, and bread crumbs.
steps: Stuff the carp with a delicate forcemeat, after thoroughly cleansing it, and sew it up to prevent the stuffing from falling out.
Rub it over with an egg, and sprinkle it with bread crumbs, lay it in a deep earthen dish, and drop the butter, oiled, over the bread crumbs.
Add the stock, onions, bay-leaf, herbs, wine, and anchovies, and bake for 1 hour.

Put 1 oz. of butter into a stewpan, melt it, and dredge in sufficient flour to dry it up; put in the strained liquor from the carp, stir frequently, and when it has boiled, add the lemon-juice and seasoning.
Serve the carp on a dish garnished with parsley and cut lemon, and the sauce in a boat.

title: Baked Damsons for Winter Use
description: Prepared with damsons, mutton, and sugar.

ingredients.name: pounded sugar per lb. of fruit
ingredients.sourceText: 6 oz. of pounded sugar per lb. of fruit

steps: Choose sound fruit, not too ripe; pick off the stalks, weigh it, and to every lb. allow 6 oz. of pounded sugar
Put the fruit into large dry stone jars, sprinkling the sugar amongst it
Cover the jars with saucers, place them in a rather cool oven, and bake the fruit until it is quite tender
When cold, cover the top of the fruit with a piece of white paper cut to the size of the jar
Pour over this melted mutton suet about an inch thick, and cover the tops of the jars with thick brown paper, well tied down
Keep the jars in a cool dry place, and the fruit will remain good till the following Christmas, but not much longer

title: Baked Gooseberry Pudding
description: A pudding made with gooseberries, bread crumbs, and puff-paste.
steps: Put the gooseberries into a jar, previously cutting off the tops and tails
Place this jar in boiling water, and let it boil until the gooseberries are soft enough to pulp
Beat them through a coarse sieve
To every pint of pulp add 3 well-whisked eggs, 1-1/2 oz. of butter, 1/2 pint of bread crumbs, and sugar to taste
Beat the mixture well
Put a border of puff-paste round the edge of a pie-dish
Put in the pudding
Bake for about 40 minutes
Strew sifted sugar over, and serve

Bake the pudding from 1 to 1-1/4 hour in a moderate oven, or boil it the same length of time in a well-buttered basin

title: Baked or Boiled Ground Rice Pudding
description: A pudding made with rice, lemon or rind or nutmeg or bitter almonds, and milk.

ingredients.name: flavouring of lemon-rind, nutmeg, bitter almonds or bay-leaf
ingredients.sourceText: flavouring of lemon-rind, nutmeg, bitter almonds or bay-leaf

steps: Put 1-1/2 pint of the milk into a stewpan, with any of the above flavourings, and bring it to the boiling-point
With the other 1/2 pint of milk, mix the ground rice to a smooth batter
Strain the boiling milk to this, and stir over the fire until the mixture is tolerably thick
Pour it into a basin, leave it uncovered, and when nearly or quite cold, sweeten it to taste, and add the eggs, which should be previously well beaten, with a little salt
For boiled pudding: Put the pudding into a well-buttered basin, tie it down with a cloth, plunge it into boiling water, and boil for 1-1/2 hour
For baked pudding: Use half the above proportion of ground rice, with the same quantity of all the other ingredients, and bake in a moderate oven for an hour
Stewed fruit, preserves, or marmalade may be served with either the boiled or baked pudding

title: Baked Pears
description: Prepared with pears, rind, and water.

ingredients.name: to every pint of water allow 1/2 lb. of loaf sugar
ingredients.sourceText: to every pint of water allow 1/2 lb. of loaf sugar

steps: Pare and cut the pears into halves, and, should they be very large, into quarters; leave the stalks on, and carefully remove the cores.

Place them in a clean baking-jar, with a closely-fitting lid; add to them the lemon-rind cut in strips, the juice of 1/2 lemon, the cloves, pounded allspice, and sufficient water just to cover the whole, with sugar in the above proportion.
Cover the jar down closely, put it into a very cool oven, and bake the pears from 5 to 6 hours, but be very careful that the oven is not too hot.
To improve the colour of the fruit, a few drops of prepared cochineal may be added; but this will not be found necessary if the pears are very gently baked.

title: Baked Soles
description: Prepared with soles, sherry, and lemon-juice.
steps: Clean, skin, and well wash the fish, and dry them thoroughly in a cloth.

title: Baked Sweetbreads
description: Prepared with sweetbreads, toast, and gravy.
steps: Choose large white sweetbreads
Put them into warm water to draw out the blood and to improve their colour
Let them remain for rather more than 1 hour
Put them into boiling water and allow them to simmer for about 10 minutes
Take them up and drain them
Brush over with egg
Sprinkle with bread crumbs

Drop on them a little oiled butter
Put the sweetbreads into a moderately-heated oven and let them bake for nearly 3/4 hour
Make 3 pieces of toast
Place the sweetbreads on the toast
Pour round, but not over them, a good brown gravy

description: Prepared with onions, mushroom, and juice.

title: Bechamel, or French White Sauce
description: A sauce made with mushrooms, stock, and cream.
steps: Put the stock into a stewpan, with the parsley, cloves, bay-leaf, herbs, and mushrooms; add a seasoning of salt, but no pepper, as that would give the sauce a dusty appearance, and should be avoided.
When it has boiled long enough to extract the flavour of the herbs, etc., strain it, and boil it up quickly again, until it is nearly half-reduced.

Now mix the arrowroot smoothly with the cream, and let it simmer very gently for 5 minutes over a slow fire; pour to it the reduced stock, and continue to simmer slowly for 10 minutes, if the sauce be thick.
If, on the contrary, it be too thin, it must be stirred over a sharp fire till it thickens.

steps: Slice and fry the onions of a pale brown, and cut up the other vegetables in small pieces.

Choose a fine piece of beef, cut the bacon into long slices, about an inch in thickness, dip them into vinegar, and then into a little of the above seasoning of spice, &c., mixed with the same quantity of minced herbs.
With a sharp knife make holes deep enough to let in the bacon.
Rub the beef over with the remainder of the seasoning and herbs, and bind it up in a nice shape with tape.
Have ready a well-tinned stewpan into which put the beef, with the vegetables, vinegar, and water.
Let it simmer very gently for 5 hours, or rather longer, should the meat not be extremely tender, and turn it once or twice.
When ready to serve, take out the beef, remove the tape, and put it on a hot dish.
Skim off every particle of fat from the gravy, add the port wine, just let it boil, and pour it over the beef.

title: Beef Fritters
description: Prepared with roast beef, lard, and onions.
steps: Mix very smoothly, and by degrees, the flour with the proportion of water.
Stir in {{source-5}}, which must be melted, but not oiled.
Just before it is to be used, add the whites of two well-whisked eggs.
Should the batter be too thick, add more water.
Pare down the cold beef into thin shreds, season with pepper and salt, and mix it with the batter.
A small quantity of finely-minced onions, mixed with the batter, is an improvement.
Drop a small quantity at a time into a pan of boiling lard, and fry from 7 to 10 minutes, according to the size.
When done on one side, turn and brown them on the other.
Let them dry for a minute or two before the fire, and serve on a folded napkin.

title: Beef-Steak and Kidney Pudding
description: A pudding made with steak, kidneys, and suet.

ingredients.name: suet to each 1 lb. of flour
ingredients.sourceText: 6 oz. of suet to each 1 lb. of flour

steps: Procure some tender rump steak (that which has been hung a little time), and divide it into pieces about an inch square, and cut each kidney into 8 pieces.
Line the dish with crust made with suet and flour in the proportion of {{source-5}}, leaving a small piece of crust to overlap the edge.
Cover the bottom with a portion of the steak and a few pieces of kidney.
Season with salt and pepper.
Add another layer of steak, kidney, and seasoning.
Proceed in this manner till the dish is full.
Pour in sufficient water to come within 2 inches of the top of the basin.
Moisten the edges of the crust, cover the pudding over, press the two crusts together, that the gravy may not escape, and turn up the overhanging paste.
Wring out a cloth in hot water, flour it, and tie up the pudding.

title: Beef-Steak Pie
description: A pastry dish made with steak, salt, and pepper.
steps: Have the steaks cut from a rump that has hung a few days, that they may be tender, and be particular that every portion is perfectly sweet.
Cut the steaks into pieces about 3 inches long and 2 wide, allowing a small piece of fat to each piece of lean, and arrange the meat in layers in a pie-dish.
Between each layer sprinkle a seasoning of salt, pepper, and, when liked, a few grains of cayenne.
Fill the dish sufficiently with meat to support the crust, and to give it a nice raised appearance when baked, and not to look flat and hollow.
Pour in sufficient water to half fill the dish, and border it with paste.
Brush it over with a little water, and put on the cover.
Slightly press down the edges with the thumb, and trim off close to the dish.
Ornament the pie with leaves, or pieces of paste cut in any shape that fancy may direct.
Brush it over with the beaten yolk of an egg.
Make a hole in the top of the crust, and bake in a hot oven for about 1-1/2 hour.

title: Beef-Steak, Rolled, Roasted, and Stuffed
description: Prepared with steak, forcemeat, and clarified butter.
steps: Have the steaks cut rather thick from a well-hung rump of beef, and sprinkle over them a seasoning of pepper and salt.

Roast it before a nice clear fire for about 1-1/2 hour, or rather longer, should the roll be very large and thick.
Keep it constantly basted with butter.
Serve with brown gravy, some of which must be poured round the steak, and the remainder sent to table in a tureen.

title: Black-Currant Jam
description: A fruit preserve made with fruit, sugar, and water.

ingredients.name: fruit, weighed before being stripped from the stalks
ingredients.sourceText: 1 lb. of fruit, weighed before being stripped from the stalks

ingredients.name: loaf sugar per lb. of fruit

ingredients.name: 1 gill of water per lb. of fruit
ingredients.sourceText: 1 gill of water per lb. of fruit

steps: Let the fruit be very ripe, and gathered on a dry day
Strip it from the stalks, and put it into a preserving-pan, with a gill of water to each lb. of fruit
Boil these together for 10 minutes

Add the sugar, and boil the jam again for 30 minutes, reckoning from the time when the jam simmers equally all over, or longer, should it not appear to set nicely when a little is poured on to a plate
Keep stirring it to prevent it from burning
Carefully remove all the scum
When done, pour it into pots
Let it cool, cover the top of the jam with oiled paper, and the top of the jars with a piece of tissue-paper brushed over on both sides with the white of an egg

description: Prepared with currants, water, and sugar.

ingredients.name: 1/4 pint of water per pint of juice
ingredients.sourceText: 1/4 pint of water per pint of juice

ingredients.name: loaf sugar per pint of juice

steps: Strip the currants from the stalks by holding the bunch in one hand, and passing a small silver fork down the currants
Put them into a jar, place this jar in a saucepan of boiling water, and simmer them until their juice is extracted

Stir these ingredients together cold until the sugar is dissolved
Place the preserving-pan on the fire, and boil the jelly for about 1/2 hour, reckoning from the time it commences to boil all over
Carefully remove the scum as it rises
When the jelly becomes firm when a little is put on a plate, it is done
Put it into small pots, and cover

title: Blanc-Mange
description: Prepared with isinglass, rind, and bitter almonds.
steps: Put the milk into a saucepan, with the isinglass, lemon-rind, and sugar, and let these ingredients stand by the side of the fire until the milk is well flavoured
Add the almonds, which should be blanched and pounded in a mortar to a paste, and let the milk just boil up
Strain it through a fine sieve or muslin into a jug, add the cream, and stir the mixture occasionally until nearly cold
Let it stand for a few minutes, then pour it into the mould, which should be previously oiled with the purest salad-oil, or dipped in cold water
Omit the sediment at the bottom of the jug when pouring into the mould
Turn it out carefully on a dish by loosening the edges from the mould, placing a dish on it, and turning it quickly over
Garnish as fancy dictates

title: Boiled Bacon
description: Prepared with bacon and water.
steps: As bacon is frequently excessively salt, let it be soaked in warm water for an hour or two previous to dressing it; then pare off the rusty parts, and scrape the under-side and rind as clean as possible.
Put it into a saucepan of cold water, let it come gradually to a boil, and as fast as the scum rises to the surface of the water, remove it.

Let it simmer very gently until it is thoroughly done; then take it up, strip off the skin, and sprinkle over the bacon a few bread raspings, and garnish with tufts of cauliflower or Brussels sprouts.
When served alone, young and tender broad beans or green peas are the usual accompaniments.

move the basin about for a few minutes after it is put into the water, to prevent the flour settling in any part, and boil for 1-1/4 hour
Send these puddings very quickly to table, and serve with sweet sauce, wine sauce, stewed fruit, or jam of any kind

title: Boiled Beetroot
description: Prepared with beetroot and water.
steps: Wash the beets thoroughly
Do not prick or break the skin before they are cooked, or they would lose their beautiful colour in boiling
Put them into boiling water and let them boil until tender, keeping them well covered
If to be served hot, remove the peel quickly, cut the beetroot into thick slices, and send to table with melted butter
For salads, pickle, etc., let the root cool, then peel and cut it into slices

title: Boiled Bread Pudding
description: A pudding made with bread crumbs, currants, and milk.
steps: Make the milk boiling, and pour it on the bread crumbs
Let these remain till cold
Add the other ingredients, taking care that the eggs are well beaten and the currants well washed, picked, and dried
Beat the pudding well, and put it into a buttered basin
Tie it down tightly with a cloth
Plunge it into boiling water, and boil for 1-1/4 hour
Turn it out of the basin, and serve with sifted sugar
Any odd pieces or scraps of bread answer for this pudding; but they should be soaked overnight, and, when wanted for use, should have the water well squeezed from them

title: Boiled Broccoli
description: Prepared with broccoli, water, and salt.
steps: Strip off the dead outside leaves, and the inside ones cut off level with the flower
Cut off the stalk close at the bottom
Put the broccoli into cold salt and water, with the heads downwards
Let them remain in this for about 3/4 hour until perfectly free from insects
Put them into a saucepan of boiling water, salted in the above proportion
Keep them boiling quickly over a brisk fire, with the saucepan uncovered
Take them up with a slice the moment they are done
Drain them well
Serve with a tureen of melted butter, a little of which should be poured over the broccoli

title: Boiled Brussels Sprouts
description: Prepared with brussels sprouts, melted butter, and water.

ingredients.name: a very small piece of soda
ingredients.sourceText: a very small piece of soda

steps: Clean the sprouts from insects and nicely wash them
Pick off any dead or discoloured leaves from the outsides
Put them into a saucepan of boiling water, with salt and soda in the above proportion
Keep the pan uncovered and let them boil quickly over a brisk fire until tender
Drain and dish
Serve with a tureen of melted butter, or with a maître d'hôtel sauce poured over them
Alternatively, when dished, stir in about 1-1/2 oz. of butter and a seasoning of pepper and salt
